chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Ali al-Ahmasi, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Worry and grief do not cease to be with the believer until they leave no sin for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of worry and grief for a believer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of 'hastening punishment' (ta'jil al-darar), where worldly anxieties and grief serve as expiatory mechanisms for a believer's sins. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that divine mercy often manifests through the removal of sin through minor afflictions in this life, sparing the believer greater retribution in the Hereafter. The narration underscores the spiritual benefit of enduring patience (sabr) during these periods of emotional distress as a means of purification.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abaas Bin Musa Al Warraq, from Ali Al Ahmasy, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The worries and the grief do not cease to be with the Momin until no sin is left for him’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-‘Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq from Ali al-Ahmasi from a man from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Anxiety and sadness continue to trouble a believer until no sin is left in him.’”
